progressMetric.label: UTR
progressMetric.description: Universal Tennis Rating — a 1–16 scale that compares your child directly against any player in the world, including the draw you are thinking of entering.

intro: How tennis actually works in India: the AITA age-group ladder, what each rung costs a family, the money available at each one, and where the ladder leads.

sources.label: Khelo India Athlete Scheme, Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports

stages.title: Discover Tennis
stages.shortDescription: Explore if tennis is right for your child
stages.summary: The honest question, before you spend anything on it.
stages.goal: Find out whether your child enjoys the game enough to keep at it for years.
stages.duration: A few months of trying it

cost.label: ₹30,000 – ₹80,000 a year
cost.note: Recreational beginner level. Indicative and variable by city and academy — not a quote.

india.schoolRoute: Most Indian children meet tennis at school or a local club rather than an academy. Both are a fine place to start and cost far less.

dos: Judge it on whether they look forward to going
avoid: Specialising in one sport this early
Buying an adult racquet because it will last longer
questionsForCoach: Do you use the ITF Tennis10s ball stages?
How many children per coach in a session?

readinessChecklist: Your child asks to go back
The coach is experienced with young children
Racquet length and ball colour suit their size
outcomes: A sport they can play socially for life
Coordination and balance that transfer to any sport

criteria: They enjoy it and want to keep going

notes: The single best predictor of how far a child goes is whether they enjoy it. A child who looks forward to practice improves for years; one who was pushed stops.

stages.title: Getting Started
stages.shortDescription: Learn the basics and build a strong start
stages.summary: Coaching on a smaller court, with a slower ball and first rallies.
stages.goal: Rally in week one rather than month six, and build the coordination everything later rests on.

india.schoolRoute: School and SGFI tennis is the cheapest match practice in India, and teaches scoring and nerves with no ranking riding on it.

dos: Watch quietly and let the coach coach
Ask what they enjoyed, not whether they won
questionsForCoach: When should we move up a ball colour?

readinessChecklist: Technique is sound across the basic strokes
They move confidently around the court
Training is balanced against school and free play
outcomes: A technical base that holds up on a full court

criteria: Rallying consistently on the orange court
movingUp.typicalDuration: After 2–3 years of red and orange ball

stages.title: First AITA Ranking
stages.shortDescription: Register with AITA and earn first ranking points
stages.summary: AITA Talent Series — U-10 and U-12, and the first points on the board.
stages.goal: Enter ranked Indian tennis with a plan, and learn what a ranking does and does not measure.

requirements: Registration through your state tennis association
registration.earliestAge: U-10 opens at age 7; most families register between 9 and 11

india.stateAssociationRole: Your state association processes registration and hosts most Talent Series events. It is the first door, not the national body.

competitionTiers.name: AITA Talent Series
competitionTiers.whoCanEnter: AITA-registered players in the age category

competitionTiers.name: SGFI school nationals
competitionTiers.whoCanEnter: Through your school, no AITA ranking needed

rankingSystem.name: AITA age-group ranking
howPointsWork: Points come from the tournament category, the round reached and match results
Higher-category tournaments award more points for the same result
Consistency over a season moves a ranking more than one good week

administrative: AITA membership and verified age proof
competitive: Can serve, rally and score a match unaided — and handle losing one

funding.name: Academy scholarships
funding.body: Private academies (RoundGlass, MS Star, IMG and similar)
funding.eligibility: Awarded on the academy's own trials, typically from this level
funding.benefit: Can waive coaching or residential fees outright
funding.howToApply: Apply directly to the academy and attend its trial

dos: Build an annual calendar with school exams in it first
avoid: Travelling long distances for low-value events
questionsForCoach: What is the objective of this tournament beyond winning?

readinessChecklist: Registered with AITA, age proof verified
Competing in age-appropriate events rather than the biggest draw
outcomes: A ranking that opens age-group draws across India

academics.note: Tournament weeks and school terms collide from here. Put exam dates in the calendar before you enter anything.

criteria: Consistent quarter-finals at Talent Series level

stages.title: National Ranking
stages.shortDescription: Compete nationally and climb the AITA ladder
stages.summary: AITA Championship and Super Series — U-14 to U-18, and a national ranking.
stages.goal: Build a national ranking that holds up, and secure the funding before the costs arrive.

cost.label: ₹3L – ₹12L a year
cost.note: Rises steeply with travel. This is where most families stop for cost reasons rather than talent reasons.

competitionTiers.name: AITA Championship Series
competitionTiers.whoCanEnter: AITA-ranked players in the age category

competitionTiers.name: AITA Super Series and Nationals
competitionTiers.whoCanEnter: Top-ranked players in the age group

rankingSystem.name: AITA national age-group ranking
whatItUnlocks: AITA nomination for ITF junior events

india.stateAssociationRole: State nomination still matters for some national draws.

competitive: AITA age-group ranking inside the top 100 to progress
Top 20 in India for international entry

funding.name: Khelo India Athlete Scheme
funding.body: Sports Authority of India / Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports
funding.eligibility: Selection typically happens around national age-group level
funding.benefit: Reported at roughly ₹6 lakh a year covering training, equipment, diet and education for as long as the athlete stays in the scheme
funding.howToApply: Selection is via Khelo India trials and national performance

funding.name: Corporate sponsorship
funding.eligibility: A national ranking is the track record sponsors want before committing
funding.benefit: Varies; the only funding that scales with the player's own story

dos: Chase the funding before the costs arrive, not after
avoid: Playing too many tournaments and training too little
Overspending without a structured annual budget
questionsForCoach: What is the written long-term development plan?

readinessChecklist: Understands the AITA tournament structure and where they sit in it
A sustainable national ranking built on consistency
An annual tournament, travel and recovery calendar
Academics, training and rest genuinely in balance
outcomes: Enough to open a university seat or a coaching career, whatever happens next
A few hundred children in the country are here in any age group

burnoutSigns: Recurring niggles that never fully settle

academics.boardExamNote: Class 10 and 12 board years fall inside the peak competition years. Plan a reduced tournament load around them rather than discovering the clash in January.
quotaRoutes: Indian university sports quota on a documented AITA age-group ranking
Fee concessions and hostel places, which differ by university

criteria: Top 20 in India in the age group
movingUp.warning: Entry to the bottom rung of professional tennis needs only an IPIN and an entry fee. The players in that draw sit around UTR 13. Entering early means first-round losses for zero points, at roughly ₹2–4 lakh a year in travel and entries — the gate in tennis is competitive, not administrative.
